title: Subagent and parallel-activity presentation strategy
objective: Define how parent-agent, subagent, team, background, and parallel tool activity should be grouped, summarized, expanded, navigated, and attributed without flooding or hiding failures.

include: Spawn, queued, running, waiting, blocked, failed, cancelled, and completed states
Actor identity, assigned objective, progress, latest meaningful event, duration, tools, token/cost, and result preview
Nested-agent limits, aggregation, event ordering, late-arriving output, and focus behavior
Permission prompts and failures originating in child agents
exclude: Agent scheduling algorithms unrelated to presentation
Full child transcript streaming as the default view
Conflating work-unit state with individual tool-call state

deliverables: A subagent card/row information contract by lifecycle state
Rules for grouping parallel work and surfacing the critical path
Accessibility, determinism, failure-escalation, and evidence-retention requirements
acceptance_criteria: The user can answer who is doing what, what changed, what failed, and how to inspect it
A single noisy subagent cannot monopolize the transcript
Errors and permission requests are promoted even when the parent group is collapsed
verification: Walk through at least one six-agent concurrent scenario with mixed outcomes

result.summary: Lifecycle, identity, attention, grouping, escalation, accessibility, and evidence contract for parallel subagent work, including a six-agent scenario.
